args.body:
File: src/util/money.ts

Extend parseAmount's symbol-stripping to cover the rupee sign (₹) and other currency symbols/prefixes (e.g. alphabetic codes like 'CHF') and accept apostrophe as a thousands separator, instead of the hardcoded regex /[\s€$£¥]/g that only strips four specific symbols.

label: bug
file: src/util/money.ts
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.
parseAmount in src/util/money.ts does `text = raw.replace(/[\s€$£¥]/g, "")` which omits ₹, so '₹1,250.00' keeps the ₹ character, fails the /^\d+(\.\d+)?$/ test, and returns null, producing the 'amount is not a number' error (src/i18n/en.json errors.badAmount); similarly 'CHF 1'200.00' keeps 'CHF' and the apostrophe separator, also failing.
